idiom_name: validity Range attached to the dated record + as-of predicate + period policy
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: give the dated fact its own record with one validity Range value (validFrom plus validUntil-or-open) and give the range three operations - contains(date), overlaps(other) and, for corrections, replaceWith(range). Reads take an explicit as-of date and filter with contains(); the write side owns the non-overlap rule: either reject an insert whose range overlaps an existing one for the same identity, or order intentional overlaps by an explicit precedence field. Keep the outcome space explicit - effective record, no record (gap), not yet effective - instead of collapsing all three into null. Fix the bound convention once and use it everywhere: half-open [from, until) with an open end is the safest default, because adjacent periods then touch without overlapping and "until further notice" needs no sentinel date.
pitfalls: Skipping the write-side rule: two overlapping periods for one identity make the as-of query return whichever record the plan reaches first - enforce non-overlap or document precedence.
Using a sentinel end date for open periods; the sentinel leaks into duration arithmetic and exports and hides the "until further notice" intent.
Filtering in application code over a full history instead of querying the range: correct but O(history) and invisible to the query planner.

Wrong move: versioning each update as a new effective-dated row with a fresh surrogate id -> child tables keep foreign keys to the superseded id and every join across related tables must re-resolve the version -> instead keep one stable identity per logical fact (only the period is new) and use a history/audit table when the real question is "what changed when", not "what was true then".

Wrong move: making every mutable table effective-dated "for safety" (an EFFDT/Effective-from-To on records that never needed history) -> every read pays a temporal predicate and a current-row concept is invented where the domain has none -> instead apply effectivity only where the domain itself understands the fact as having a period; PeopleTools' own guidance is to use EFFDT exclusively on records that genuinely maintain history.

Wrong move: fabricating an Effective To for open-ended facts by back-dating it to the day before the next row -> the manufactured end breaks whenever a legitimate gap exists and turns absent data into a false deadline -> instead leave the open end genuinely open (NULL) and store closed from/to dates only where the domain really knows the end, as the warehouse literature (insurance dual dates versus retail until-superseded prices) distinguishes.
